cohort: The study included 100 women undergoing emergency caesarean deliveries, divided into spinal anaesthesia (n=50) and general anaesthesia (n=50) groups.
finding: Spinal anaesthesia resulted in significantly higher Quality of Recovery (QoR-40) scores and longer total operation time compared to general anaesthesia, with no significant difference in pain and satisfaction scores (VAS, NRS) between the groups.
mod_finding: For emergency caesarean deliveries, spinal anaesthesia was associated with better quality of recovery but also longer operation time compared to general anaesthesia, without affecting patient satisfaction or pain scores.
